title: Tenali Raman and the Stolen Golconda Diamond

full_text:
A priceless uncut blue diamond from the mines of Golconda, kept in the King’s private gemological cabinet, vanished during an inventory audit.
The room had three keys, held by the three Chief Vault Keepers: Somadatta, Bheema, and Ramanathan.
All three men were searched immediately: their clothes, their shoes, and their lockers contained nothing.
All three swore upon their sacred threads that they were innocent.

King Krishnadevaraya, desperate to recover the crown jewel, called Tenali Raman.
Tenali said: 'Maharaj, the thief had no time to carry the diamond outside the palace walls, for the alarm was sounded within ten minutes of the theft.
The diamond is still hidden within this room.
Give me until midnight, and the thief will deliver the gem into my hand.'

Tenali had the room locked from the outside, leaving the three keepers inside with food and water.
Tenali had a small, concealed peephole drilled through the wooden ceiling beam, allowing him to watch the room from the attic above.

At midnight, Tenali leaned through the peephole and whispered in a low, mysterious, spectral tone that echoed through the stone chamber:
'Somadatta... Bheema... Ramanathan...
The King has ordered the master masons to arrive at dawn with sledgehammers!
They will break open the stone floor, dismantle the fireplace, and smash the carved wooden pillars to find the diamond!
Whoever hid the diamond behind the hollow brick in the hearth will see it found and lose his head!'

The three keepers leaped up from their cots in the dark.
Two of the keepers sat back down, confused by the strange voice.
However, the third keeper, Ramanathan, turned pale with terror!
He thought: 'Heavens! How did the King discover my secret hiding place behind the hearth?'

Panicking in the dark, Ramanathan crept silently to the large stone fireplace.
He reached his hand up the chimney flue, pulled away a loose soot-covered brick, took out the blue diamond wrapped in wax paper, and tried to slip it into his turban!

At that moment, Tenali Raman kicked open the heavy door, carrying a bright lantern and backed by royal guards!
'Hold, Ramanathan! Thou hast found the diamond for us!'

Ramanathan dropped the soot-covered gem, falling to his knees in utter confession.
The King was amazed at how Tenali’s phantom whisper had caused the thief to unmask his own cache.
The Golconda diamond was restored to the crown, Ramanathan was sentenced to restorative labor, and Tenali was rewarded with a gold medallion for his brilliant psychological deduction.
moral: A thief's secret stash is unearthed when suspicion is cast upon the only man who knows the hiding place.
